operational-example.copy: Use Table when users need to compare structured records by columns, sort values, and inspect row-level detail.

scenario.title: Fleet spend table

items.label: Vehicle spend
items.description: Compare plate, driver, status, and spend.

items.label: Sorted spend
items.description: Sort by amount before investigating exceptions.

items.label: Expandable row
items.description: Open a row to inspect recent activity.

rationale: Table supports scanning and comparison better than cards when records share the same fields.
The ZIP reference uses a card surface, sunken header, compact overline headers, sortable arrows, selected rows, and optional detail rows.
Use it for structured records; use List or Card when comparison is not the main task.

items.rule: Wraps the table in a stable card surface.
Names columns and exposes sort controls when sortable.
Show comparable records with consistent alignment.
Marks selected rows without changing column meaning.
Optional secondary row for row-specific detail.

accessibility.statePrecedence: expanded, selected, sorted, focus, hover, default
items: Use table semantics for comparable records.
Use scope col on column headers.
Keep row actions keyboard reachable without making the whole table ambiguous.
Do not use Table for layout-only grids.

variants.copy: Table variants describe comparison density and interaction: standard, dense, sortable, selectable, and expandable.

states.copy: Table states communicate row focus, hover, selected records, sorted columns, expanded detail, and default availability.

variant-state-behavior.copy: Variant defines the table capability; state identifies the current sort, selection, focus, hover, or detail expansion.

full-width.copy: Table usually fills its container so columns can breathe; avoid forcing many columns into narrow cards.

responsive-layout-patterns.copy: Use Table where the viewport can support column comparison. On phones, reduce columns or escalate to a list pattern.

viewport-organization.copy: Keep Table for comparison tasks. Use List on constrained phones and Drawer or Dialog for row detail when expansion becomes too heavy.

items.title: Phone
items.rule: Use reduced columns or a list pattern.

items.title: Tablet
items.rule: Keep key columns visible and move row detail behind expansion.

items.title: Desktop
items.rule: Use sorting, selection, and detail rows for high-volume comparison.

playground.copy: Use the playground to verify variant, state, density, sort behavior, selected row, and expandable detail.

api-foundations.copy: Table API exposes columns, rows, row identity, sorting, selection, expansion, and density while Design System foundations own surface, spacing, typography, focus, and accessibility.

props.name: columns
props.notes: Column definitions with label, key, align, mono, render, and sort behavior.

props.name: state
props.type: default | hover | focus | selected | sorted | expanded

props.name: onSortChange
props.notes: Called when local sort is requested.

props.name: onRowSelect
props.notes: Called when a row is selected.

groups.title: Use
items: Align numbers right and identifiers consistently.

groups.title: Avoid
items: Do not use as a layout grid.
Do not force many columns into phones.
Do not hide row actions without keyboard access.

groups.title: Review
items: Check headers, aria-sort, focus, row selection, expansion, and reduced columns.

rejectIf: Table is used only for layout.
Rows cannot be identified by stable keys.

miel.copy: MIEL treats Table as structured comparison: agents can build columns and rows when the schema is clear, while humans confirm priority, privacy, and row actions.
canDecide: Use Table for repeated records with shared fields.
Use sortable columns for comparable metrics.
Use expandable detail when row context is secondary.
mustAsk: Bulk or destructive row actions are needed.
rejectIf: A table is used for decorative layout.
Sort, selection, or expansion behavior is fake.
Row identity and keyboard behavior are undefined.
miel.handoff: I am using Table for record comparison. Please confirm columns, row identity, sortable fields, selection rules, and what happens on constrained viewports.
